title: Paul planted, Apollos watered (1 Corinthians 3:1–9)
tomorrow: where does God live? Paul's answer isn't a building.

cards: A banquet at the end of the season, and the argument starts: who actually built this team? Corinth is having that fight about two teachers. Paul answers: "I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase."
Then he says something odd. The planter isn't anything. The waterer isn't anything.
And in the very next verse, each one gets a reward for his own work. Nothing, and rewarded?

teach.b: Start with the setup. Paul says he's had to feed them like babies: "I have fed you with milk, and not with meat". The sign they're not ready? "envying, and strife, and divisions."
So he takes the two names they fight over and makes them small: "Who then is Paul, and who is Apollos, but ministers by whom ye believed". Helpers.
Then the odd line: "So then neither is he that planteth any thing, neither he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase." Here's the answer to the puzzle. Not any thing is about the growth.
A gardener can't make a seed sprout; that part was never theirs.
But the work is real, and so is the reward: "he that planteth and he that watereth are one: and every man shall receive his own reward according to his own labour."
Nothing, as the source of growth.
Something, as a worker. And not rivals: one.
"For we are labourers together with God: ye are God's husbandry, ye are God's building."
Husbandry is the old word for farming, here a farmed field. Which puts the people who worked your field before you, and the ones who'll work it after, on the same side.

how: Some churches remember the people who founded and served them, naming earlier pastors, teachers and members, and read 1 Corinthians 3 when a new minister begins.

games.q: your team wins state. the new coach gets all the praise, but the old coach built the program. what fits 1 Corinthians 3?
o: thank both, and remember neither made the players grow.
praise the new coach; results are what count in the end.
praise the old coach; whoever starts it deserves the credit.
games.why: planter and waterer are one, each rewarded for the work, and the increase comes from God. no rivalry, no ranking.

practice: Bring to mind one person who planted something in you before you noticed: a teacher, a grandparent, a coach. Send them one line of thanks that names what they planted.
Then put the phone down and sit with the growth that came after.

wordCard.voice: Paul planted. One gardener among others: he planted, Apollos watered, and the growth came from God.

orig.note: Greek: to grow, to make grow. In 1 Corinthians 3:6, God gave the increase.

carryVoice: Hold onto this: God gives the growth, and the planters still count. See you tomorrow.
